description: MD Fit Pain Tool mappings - Dr. Jared can edit this file to manage body region to exercise mappings

mappings.name: Scalene/Neck Tension
red_flags: Numbness or tingling down arm that persists
mappings.educational_content: The scalene muscles run along the side of your neck and can refer pain to the chest, shoulder, and arm when tight. This pattern is often mistaken for heart or shoulder problems. The scalenes can also compress nerves and blood vessels going to the arm (thoracic outlet). Gentle release work, postural improvements, and breathing exercises typically help.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Rotator Cuff (Infraspinatus)
mappings.educational_content: The infraspinatus is a rotator cuff muscle on the back of your shoulder blade. When tight or irritated, it can refer pain deep into the front of the shoulder and down the outside of the arm. External rotation exercises and gentle stretching help restore balance. Improving thoracic mobility often reduces shoulder stress.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Upper Back / Thoracic Stiffness
mappings.educational_content: The thoracic spine should rotate and extend freely. When stiff, it can cause local pain and also refer discomfort around the ribs and into the chest. Upper back stiffness often contributes to neck and shoulder problems. Rotation exercises and extension work typically provide relief.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Lower Back (QL) Pain
red_flags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Severe pain that doesn't improve with any position
mappings.educational_content: The quadratus lumborum (QL) connects your pelvis to your spine and ribs. When tight, it can cause deep low back and hip pain, often worse on one side. QL issues often respond well to hip mobility work, gentle spinal movement, and core stabilization.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Hip Flexor / Psoas Pain
mappings.educational_content: The psoas connects your spine to your leg and is the primary hip flexor. When tight from sitting, it can pull on the lower back and cause pain. The psoas also affects breathing and nervous system function. Hip flexor stretching and core work typically help.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Hip / Lateral Hip Pain
red_flags: Hip giving way or feeling unstable
mappings.educational_content: The glute minimus can cause pain that mimics sciatica, referring down the outside of the leg to the ankle. This 'pseudo-sciatica' pattern is common and often responds well to hip strengthening (especially glute medius) and mobility work.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Groin / Inner Hip Pain
mappings.educational_content: Groin pain can originate from multiple structures including the hip flexors (psoas, iliacus), adductors, or the hip joint itself. The psoas can refer pain to the front of the hip and inner thigh. Hip rotation exercises and hip flexor lengthening often provide relief.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Hamstring / Back of Thigh Pain
red_flags: Sudden severe pain with pop sound
mappings.educational_content: Hamstring pain can originate from the muscle itself or be referred from the glutes, lower back, or sciatic nerve. Often, strengthening the glutes reduces hamstring strain by improving load distribution. Romanian deadlifts help build hamstring capacity when pain allows.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Calf / Heel Pain
red_flags: Complete inability to walk on toes
mappings.educational_content: The soleus can refer pain to the heel and bottom of the foot, often mimicking plantar fasciitis. The calf muscles and plantar fascia work together in a kinetic chain. Eccentric calf exercises are evidence-based treatment for both calf and Achilles issues, and often help plantar fascia symptoms as well.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Plantar Fasciitis / Heel Pain
mappings.educational_content: Plantar fasciitis causes heel pain, typically worst with first steps in the morning. The plantar fascia is connected to the calf muscles through the Achilles tendon, forming a continuous fascial line. Both calf stretching/strengthening and direct plantar fascia work are typically needed for full recovery. Most cases resolve with consistent exercise over 6-12 weeks.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Side / Oblique Pain
mappings.educational_content: The external and internal obliques help rotate and side-bend your trunk. They can refer pain to the lower abdomen and groin area. Core stabilization exercises help restore function, followed by gradual return to rotational activities.
mappings.disclaimer: This tool is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. If you are experiencing severe pain, numbness, weakness, or other concerning symptoms, please consult a healthcare professional immediately.

mappings.name: Chest Wall / Pec Pain
red_flags: Chest pain with shortness of breath
Pain radiating to jaw or left arm
mappings.educational_content: The pectoralis muscles can refer pain to the front of the shoulder and down the arm. IMPORTANT: Always rule out cardiac causes for chest pain before assuming muscular origin. If you experience chest pain with exertion, shortness of breath, or other concerning symptoms, seek medical evaluation first. Muscular chest wall pain typically improves with thoracic mobility work and postural correction.
